id: D-181 S01 plate + invisible pedestal proxy (supersedes the shaded pedestal of D-179)
units: metres, three.js Y-up (glTF). Pedestal origin = centre of its bottom face, on the desk plane y = 0.

pedestal.role: PROXY (D-181): invisible. material.colorWrite = false, depthWrite = true (occludes the ring), plus a multiply shadow catcher (PCSS) on the same mesh for the ring's shadow. Do NOT shade it: the pedestal the user sees is in the plate.
pedestal.castShadow_note: the pedestal's own shadow on the desk is baked into the plate; if the proxy also cast it, the desk catcher would darken it twice. Ring: castShadow true.

ring.note: position/quaternion already assume s01_scale. ring leans back-right resting on its lower edge (lowest vertex at top_y), opening toward camera-right, logo lower-left front (Figma 40004725:5602). Blender axis (-0.72, 0.5, -0.48), logo dir (-0.7, -0.55, -0.45)

filmOffset_or_viewOffset.note: unchanged from D-179: Blender shift_y 0.135 of the frame width moves the subject down (heroBg.cam.shiftY).

plate.note: RECALIBRATED AGAINST THE UPSCALED PLATE (D-181): the 3632 x 2072 upscale is the 1818 x 1037 source stretched to the full frame (measured u = 1.99768 x - 0.09, v = 1.99800 y + 0.03, 0.3 px rms), so every frame FRACTION is unchanged and heroBg.cam {frameW 1818, frameH 1037, focalPx 70/36*1818, shiftY 0.135} stays valid: keep those numbers and lay the plate out with the photo's cover box. u = 0.5 + f*x_c/-z_c, v = pp_v - f*(1818/1037)*y_c/-z_c with f = focal_fraction_of_width. The plate's own pixel ratio (3632/2072) differs from 1818/1037 by 0.014 % = 0.25 px at 3632; ignore it.

camera.frame: photo/plate frame, shown object-fit: cover, centred (desktop 1440x900 crops the sides)

check_points.note: world points (three.js Y-up, metres, pedestal space) and where they fall in the plate (u right, v down, fractions of the frame). Use them to assert the web camera.

key.convention: three.js Y-up metres in pedestal space (= Blender (x, y, z) -> (x, z, -y)). Verified against the Cycles light: Blender key at (0.190, 0.120, 0.250) m aimed at (0, 0, 0.004); a Cycles SUN with this exact direction gives the same front-left shadow as the area light (renders/s01-pedestal/s01-key-area-vs-sun.png). Light travels (-0.570, -0.738, +0.360): left, down, toward the camera (+Z), so the ring shadow on the top runs LEFT-FRONT and is ~0.9 x the casting height long (elevation 47.6 deg).

shadow.note: Cycles area light D55 mm at 333 mm = 9.4 deg penumbra cone: contact-hard at the ring's touch point, ~3-4 mm soft at the shadow tip. With VSM (uniform blur) keep the blur small (~0.5 mm = 6 texels at 2048 over +-0.045 m) so the shadow stays clearly defined, as the user asked; do not raise radius to fake the tip softness.

key.plate_note: the plate was lit with this same key (Cycles area disk D55 mm at Blender (0.190, 0.120, 0.250) m), so the live ring shadow continues the baked pedestal shadow: same direction, same 9.4 deg penumbra cone.

fill.note: no front fill; keep key:fill high so the shadow on the top reads strong (Cycles key-only vs env-only: the env adds a soft overall lift, it does not cast the shaped shadow)

lights.environment: env/v2-env-paper.exr tinted warm (#FFB87A multiply), intensity ~0.28 for ring reflections

desk.note: transparent shadow catcher over the plate; receives the RING shadow only (the pedestal's own contact shadow, AO and bounce are in the plate).

proven: Cycles: plate, stills, overlays and the proxy overlay in renders/s01-plate/ use exactly these values; the camera numbers above were re-projected with three.js-style maths and agree with Blender to 0.001 px at 1818.
proposed: three.js material flags for the proxy and the catcher opacity are a starting point, untested in web-v2 (the 3D Designer does not touch it). Match the live ring shadow density to plate/still-s01-3632.png.

transform.formula: p' = O + 0.62 (p - O) + (0, -0.14 H), O = (0.5 W, 0.86 H), over the untouched photo
transform.how: rendered natively: a 2D similarity of a pinhole image is the same camera with lens x 0.62 and a new shift, so the phone passes are separate Cycles renders (pedestal RGBA, desk shadow/bounce ratio, ring RGBA), not resampled. Geometrically identical to the CSS scale + translate of the desktop layers; the ring shadow that leaves the bottom of the desktop frame is complete here.

layers.note: desktop frame. plate = pedestal_rgba over (photo x desk_multiply). The multiply PNG is clamped at 1 (the few % of warm bounce next to the lit side exist only in the plates, which are composited in linear light).

plate.identity: still == plate with ring-overlay composited source-over in sRGB (pixel-exact up to 8-bit rounding), so poster = plate + overlay.
plate.ring_shadow_in_overlay: colour #2A1608 (the web catcher colour), straight alpha chosen so plate*(1-a) + c*a has the luminance of the exact Cycles render with the ring shadow, on the desk AND on the pedestal top/lip/front.
